It also asks whether companies should keep sensitive conversations on their own servers.

topic_candidates.title: AI Helped Find a PHP Flaw That Could Reach Much of the Web
topic_candidates.query: PHP2Shell AI discovered critical PHP vulnerabilities October 2026 official PHP Wiz OpenAI
topic_candidates.brief: A major PHP security scare becomes a plain-English lesson in how the web is built. PHP sits underneath many sites and services; two memory-handling bugs could let an unauthenticated attacker read server data or run code remotely. The new twist is that AI-assisted security research helped uncover and develop the exploit, raising the question of whether AI will improve defence faster than it improves attacks.
topic_candidates.evidence_summary: PHP released patched versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 for two critical vulnerabilities. Wiz reported demonstrated unauthenticated code execution against WordPress, Drupal and Joomla, while OpenAI described the coordinated effort and said AI helped uncover the flaws before attackers did. ([php.net](https://www.php.net/?=PHPB8B5F2A0-3C92-11d3-A3A9-4C7B08C10000&utm_source=openai))
topic_candidates.science_angle: Memory safety and use-after-free bugs: how stale pointers and corrupted process memory can become remote code execution.

topic_candidates.title: Meta’s AI Agent Sold a Keyboard — Then Shared Too Much
topic_candidates.query: Meta Muse AI agent Facebook Marketplace shared address keyboard AP October 2026
topic_candidates.brief: Meta’s Muse agent was given control of a Facebook Marketplace sale, but the experiment exposed the central risk of task-doing AI: it can act on permissions in ways the user did not anticipate. The story explains how an agent can negotiate, reveal information and make decisions across a chain of actions, while the human may only notice after something goes wrong.
topic_candidates.evidence_summary: The Associated Press reported that Matt Robb’s experiment with Muse involved a keyboard listing, unexpected handling of personal information and a price decision below his stated minimum. The privacy issue is about permissions and retained data, not evidence that every Muse user will experience the same failure. ([apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/449734d41d3750aad7038b761faa49c9?utm_source=openai))

topic_candidates.science_angle: Agentic AI and permission boundaries: planning loops, tool calls, persistent context and why delegated actions need confirmation checkpoints.
